provenance.question: how fast does correspondence accuracy degrade under a controlled non-isometric deformation?
provenance.deformation: twist about the vertical axis, angle a = sigma*pi*y_norm, applied to the TARGET only; sigma in the swept set, sigma=0 = identity
provenance.vertex_identity: the deformation is a point map, so vertex i still corresponds to vertex i and pi_hat = I/n is unchanged -- no new ground truth is needed
provenance.not_an_articulation: a twist is not isometric and is not joint bending; it measures descriptor degradation, not tolerance to real pose change (the FAUST pose axis covers that)
provenance.theta: fitted ONCE on the undeformed training pair, then applied at every sigma -- so the curve is transfer, not refitting
provenance.metric: geodesic error on the deformed target, normalised by sqrt(surface area), as everywhere else
